 Oral Judgment

(PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ASHOK S. KINAGI)
1.
These appeals arise out of the judgment and award dated 02.02.2021 passed in MVC No.8/2020 by the Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal XIV, Mudhol.

entities.text: Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal XIV, Mudhol
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Brief facts leading rise to the filing of these appeals are as follows:
3. The petitioner met with an accident and sustained grievous injuries and the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the tractor bearing registration No.KA.34/T-5528.
The petitioner filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation on account of the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.
Accordingly, prays to allow the claim petition.

4. Respondent No.1-the owner of the tractor filed a statement of objections admitting the ownership of the offending vehicle and also contended that the said vehicle was insured with the insurance company and the driver was possessing a valid and effective driving licence as on the date NC:
2026:KHC-D:3600 HC-KAR of the accident.
Hence, on these grounds prays to dismiss the claim petition against the owner of the tractor.

5. The insurance company-respondent No.2 of the tractor filed a statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition and contended that the driver of the tractor was not possessing a valid and effective driving licence as of the date of the accident and there is violation of the policy conditions.

Hence, on these grounds prays to dismiss the claim petition against the insurance company.
6.
The Tribunal, based on the rival pleadings of the parties, framed the relevant issues.
7. The claimant to substantiate his claim examined himself as PW.1 and marked 29 documents as Exs.P-1 to P-29.
The claimantexamined the Doctor through Court Commissioner as CW.1 and marked 2 documents as Ex.C.1 and C.2.

In rebuttal, respondent No.2-insurance company examined its Senior Assistant as RW.1 wherein due to typographical mistake, it is shown as CW.2 and marked 1 document as Ex.R.1 but it has been wrongly shown as Ex.C.3.

sentences.text: 3 8 . The Tribunal after assessing the verbal and documentary evidence, allowed the claim petition in part with costs of Rs.1,000/- and awarded compensation of Rs.3,97,832/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit and held respondent Nos.1 and 2 jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation and directed respondent No.2-insurer of the tractor to deposit the award amount.

9. The insurance company filed MFA No.100523/2022 and the claimant filed an appeal in MFA No.100198/2023 challenging the very same judgment and award passed in MVC No.8/2020 on the ground of quantum of compensation.

10. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the claimant and the learned counsel for the insurance company.
11.
Learned counsel for the claimant submtis that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
Hence, on this ground he prays to allow the petition filed by the claimant and to dismiss the appeal filed by the insurance company.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3600 HC-KAR 12.
Per contra, learned counsel for the insurance company submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is exorbitant and requires interference at the hands of this Court.
Hence, prays to reduce the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
Accordingly, prays to dismiss the appeal filed by the claimant and to allow the appeal filed by the insurance company.

13. Perused the records and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.
14.
The point that would arise for consideration is regarding quantum of compensation.

15. It is an undisputed fact that the claimant met with an accident and sustained grievous injuries and the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the tractor and a charge sheet was filed against the driver of the tractor marked as Ex.P-6.
The Tribunal was justified in recording a finding that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending tractor.

NC: 2026:KHC-D:3600 HC-KAR Regarding quantum of compensation:
16.
The claimant contended that he was aged 54 years as of the date of the accident and he was working as a labourer in the sugar factory and earning Rs.21,374/-.
To establish that the claimant was drawing the salary, has produced the salary certificate marked as Ex.P-27 to P.29.
The Tribunal considering Exs.P-27 to P-29, has taken the income of the claimant at Rs.19,839/-.

The claimant to prove the disability, has examined the Doctor as CW.1 who has examined the claimant clinically and radiologically and issued the disability certificate marked as Ex.C.2 wherein he has opined that the claimant has suffered a permanent physical disability to an extent of 35% to the right lower limb and 5% to the right upper limb.
The Tribunal has assessed the disability at 13%.

4 justified in taking the income of the deceased as per Ex.P-27 to 29 at Rs.19,839/- and also considering the evidence of CW.1, has rightly assessed the disability at 13% which is just and proper.

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Soni Sharma v. Oriental Insurance Company Limited and Others1 has held that, in a profession demanding highest standard of physical 2026 ACJ 109 NC:
2026:KHC-D:3600 HC-KAR fitness and endurance any impairment or disability has a direct bearing on earning capacity and career prospects; continuation in service is not determinative while assessing loss of future earning capacity.

entities.text: Soni Sharma v. Oriental Insurance Company Limited and Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the proposition of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Soni Sharma referred supra, the Tribunal was justified in granting the compensation of Rs.2,78,540/- under the head loss of future income.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal on all other heads is just and proper.
Hence, I do not find error in the impugned judgment and award.

17. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The appeals are dismissed.
Amount in deposit and the TCR be transmitted to the Tribunal concerned forthwith.
